LAREDO, Texas — Laredo officials agree the city needs a children’s hospital — but how to get one built is far from settled, according to KGNS, which surveyed the debate this week.

A non-binding ballot measure asks voters whether they support the idea, and some council members say a ‘yes’ vote would show community backing for the project. But funding looms as one of the biggest hurdles, especially with potential cuts to Medicaid and Medicare on the table.

Staffing is another challenge: pediatric specialists are in short supply nationwide, and Laredo is short on them, KGNS reported, quoting District 6 Council Member Dr. Tyler King. Some council members also worry the ballot language sets expectations too high without a clear plan behind it.

City leaders want Webb County at the table and are considering a task force to tackle the financing question — leaving the path forward, for now, unresolved.

Sources: KGNS reporting by Emma Galle (Oct. 22, 2026).

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: A non-binding ballot measure asks voters if they back a children's hospital. KGNS reports council members agree on the need but split on funding, staffing, and whether the ballot language overpromises.
title: Laredo officials agree a children's hospital is needed — but the path to building one is unclear
